title: Token Seven
logline: Sub-Inspector Nandini Joshi waits her turn with token seven at a police station she has never heard of, in a shut cinema across the railway line. She reports it and is ordered to have its 'Inspector' in her lockup before ten tomorrow; then his thickest file shows that all thirty complaints against Bhaiyaji were first turned away by her own SHO.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut; 'thana', 'FIR', 'SI', 'SHO', 'DSP sahab', 'madam', 'lockup', 'malkhana' and 'arre' kept as they are said in India.
script_note: Indian English. Spoken text is subtitle text with the square-bracket tags removed.

characters.name: Nandini Joshi
characters.role: LEAD. Sub-Inspector, six weeks into her first posting, second-in-command at the Imlipur thana. Has not written one FIR since she arrived; her own transfer application is pending with the DSP.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall (about 170 cm), lean, very straight-backed. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, level dark-brown eyes, firm mouth. Black hair, clean centre parting, low ponytail to the shoulder blades. No make-up, no bindi, no jewellery, no watch. Approved force uniform, crisp: sandy khaki shirt, two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves; dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars; white lantern on a round teal patch on each upper sleeve; khaki trousers; black belt with a black handcuff pouch on her right hip; black shoes; blue ballpoint pen clipped in her left chest pocket. No cap, no stars. Cherry-red open-face scooter helmet under her left arm when outdoors or just arrived.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Indian English with a neutral, educated small-city north-Indian accent; not British, not American. Keeps 'madam', 'thana', 'FIR', 'SI' and 'lockup' as Indian police say them. Quick, clipped. Under pressure she gets quieter, slower and more exact, never louder. Dry, not sarcastic.

characters.name: Sudhir Nirala
characters.role: Calls himself Inspector. Former booking clerk of the shut Roopam Talkies, failed the police entrance nine times, runs a thana of his own in its lobby.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short (about 160 cm), narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, neat black pencil moustache. Home-stitched copy of the force uniform, over-starched and ONE SIZE TOO BIG: shoulder seams droop, sleeves end at his knuckles, collar stands away from his neck, belt tail hangs loose. Teal epaulettes with three off-white bars; lantern sleeve patches. THE ONLY PEAKED CAP IN THE SERIES: khaki, teal band, shiny black peak, no badge, dead level. One large home-made medal above his left chest pocket: a blank brass-yellow disc as wide as his palm on a broad maroon-and-off-white striped ribbon. Brown leather holster with a buttoned flap on his right hip, never opened in this episode.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, forty, light careful tenor. Careful, slightly old-fashioned Indian English learnt from manuals, small-town north-Indian accent; not British, not American. 'Kindly', complete sentences, no contractions; police words pronounced with great care. Unhurried, courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes: the comedy is that he means it. Says 'madam' at the end of sentences.

characters.name: Dayashankar Tripathi
characters.role: Inspector, SHO Imlipur. Two years without an FIR and a zero-crime shield for it.
characters.look: Indian man, 56, large, heavy and slow, about 175 cm, big soft belly. Warm-brown skin, bald dome with a grey fringe at the sides, heavy jowls, clean-shaven, half-closed sleepy eyes. Approved uniform worn slack: khaki half-sleeve shirt, top two buttons open over a white vest, teal epaulettes with three off-white bars, lantern patches. Red-and-white checked gamchha over his LEFT shoulder. A paper cone of roasted peanuts in his LEFT hand, shells on the desk. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, mid-fifties, deep, slow, comfortable baritone, often speaking round a mouthful. Slow Indian English with a strong eastern-UP Hindi accent, never crisp; keeps the Hindi filler 'arre'. Not British, not American. Avuncular and lazy; ends arguments by offering food. Under pressure he stops chewing and goes flat and low; he does not shout.

characters.name: Pushpa Kumari
characters.role: Head Constable, twenty-six years at the Imlipur thana. Knits through every shift.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short (about 152 cm) and solid. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low. Grey-streaked black hair in a tight high bun with TWO STEEL KNITTING NEEDLES pushed through it in a cross. Approved uniform, teal epaulettes with ONE off-white bar, lantern patches. Hand-knitted plum-purple cardigan over it, open, two sagging pockets, a ball of orange wool in the right pocket. Cloth knitting bag over her left shoulder outdoors. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Plain, unhurried Indian English with a small-town north-Indian accent; not British, not American. Short sentences; keeps 'madam' and 'DSP sahab'. Says the important thing in the fewest words. Never surprised. Warmth shows only as dryness.

characters.name: DSP Anil Rathore
characters.role: The sub-division's DSP. Holds a press conference at the Imlipur thana at ten tomorrow for its second zero-crime year. Phone voice only in this episode.
characters.look: Not seen in this episode. Voice only, through the real thana's desk phone.
characters.voice_note: Same voice as the Hinglish cut. Male, late forties, bright, quick, clipped baritone; always half addressing the press. Fluent, brisk officer's Indian English with an urban north-Indian accent; not British, not American. Impatient, gives orders as times and places. Phone-filtered in the mix and must stay fully intelligible.

location: Imlipur, a small fictional town cut in two by a railway line: the lobby of the shut Roopam Talkies (the fake thana), the railway crossing with its tea stall, the real Imlipur thana, and the talkies' projection room.
time_of_day: Day 1. About 11 a.m. in the talkies (b1 to b4); about 12:30 p.m. at the crossing and the real thana (b5 to b9); about 2 p.m. back at the talkies and up in the projection room (b10 to b12). Clocks in frame have hands and no numerals.

beats.action: COLD OPEN, no establishing shot. One still from 0 s, the hook: a tight insert of a khaki sleeve with the round teal lantern patch, and Nandini's right hand holding a square grey cardboard token on a loop of string (painted blank; overlay ov_token_7: '7'). Pose: she sits with her right elbow on her knee, forearm raised, the token hanging from her fingers beside the lantern patch on her right upper sleeve; frame from just below the shoulder seam to the fingertips, so neither the epaulette nor her face is in it. Behind it, soft, the worn wooden edge of a complainants' bench and dusty high-window light. No face, no epaulette, no stars in this frame. In the silence before the line a rubber stamp comes down off screen (sound only). l01 plays over the same still: Nirala is a voice from the desk, off screen. STATE: token in her right hand; red helmet under her left arm, out of frame.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Next! Token number seven.

beats.action: Shot 1, l02: Nandini rises from the bench into a medium single, red helmet under her left arm, token in her right fist; the two off-white bars on her teal epaulettes read for the first time. Shot 2, l03, her eyeline: at the desk (the old booking counter) a small man in a too-big uniform and a dead-level peaked cap, the big brass medal on his chest, squares a stamped receipt (painted blank) onto a neat stack. At the picture-right edge, the back of the complainant with token six walks away toward the doors: a back only, never a face. STATE: tea kettle and two glasses on the counter; rubber stamp and tin ink pad by his right hand.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] I'm the SI for this area.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] And this thana is not in my records at all.

beats.action: Silent first: shot 1, close on Nirala, his eyes going to the two bars on her shoulder; not alarmed. Shot 2, the first wide of the room, held under l04: he pours tea into a glass on the counter. Now the room reads: the desk is a cinema booking counter, the film-poster frames on the walls hold faded, wordless poster art (sun-bleached colour blocks and silhouetted figures, no text, no readable face; no overlay), a hand-painted board hangs behind him (painted blank; overlay ov_fake_board, dressing only), and picture-right behind him the ticket booth with its arched grille is the lockup. Two round pillars, terrazzo floor, a wall clock with hands and no numerals.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] Kindly sit, madam. First tea, then complaint.

beats.action: She does not sit; the tea glass stands untouched on the counter between them. Shot 1, l05: two-shot across the counter, Nandini standing picture-left, Nirala picture-right; he gives his name and rank without blinking. Shot 2, l06: close on Nandini. Shot 3, l07: insert from her eyeline of his peaked cap, the only cap in the series. Shot 4, l08: close on Nirala, a pen raised helpfully over a blank complaint form (painted blank). After l08, one still with sound (0.8 s): her back going out through the lobby doors, the token still in her right fist, helmet under her left arm.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Inspector Sudhir Nirala. Imlipur Thana, this side of the line.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [deadpan] Imlipur has only one thana. Mine.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] And our force doesn't even have caps.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] Then kindly dictate, madam: 'Thana has been stolen.'

beats.action: No dialogue. Geography in one wide still: Nandini on her scooter, red helmet on, waiting at the lowered red-and-white gate arm by the tea stall (tin roof on bamboo poles, a bench, a blackened kettle; the keeper is hands on the kettle only, never a face). Behind her, small, the shut talkies, reading as a cinema front: a deep porch under a blank marquee board (painted blank, no overlay); ahead, across the single track, the town and her own thana. A train horn and the rumble of a train passing are sound only: no train in frame. Second still: insert of her right hand on the handlebar, the token's string looped round her fingers; she is looking at it.

Cut in mid-report: she has just told him. Shot 1, silent, 1.0 s: the empty, dusty complainants' bench by the doorway, held long enough to read (planted for s2a03's final image). Shot 2, l09 first half: Tripathi at the SHO's desk under the zero-crime shield (brass plate painted blank; overlay ov_shield: 'ZERO CRIME'), gamchha over his left shoulder, the paper cone of peanuts in his left hand, shells on the desk; he does not get up. Nandini stands picture-left, helmet under her left arm. Shot 3, on 'Shield देखिए': insert of the shield with a peanut pointing up at it from the bottom of frame. Shot 4, l10: close on Tripathi holding the cone out toward her; she does not take one. STATE from here to b12: the token's string looped round her right wrist, the token hanging below it.

lines.speaker: tripathi
lines.text: [chuckles] Arre, talkies? Two years, not one FIR. Zero crime. Look at the shield.

lines.speaker: tripathi
lines.text: [calm] Where there's no complaint, there's no crime. Have some peanuts.

beats.action: Three people, shot as singles and a two-shot (never three sheet faces in one frame). Shot 1, l11: single on Pushpa at the side table, knitting, needles crossed in her bun, spectacles low; she does not look up. Beside her wool lies an envelope with a receipt stamp (painted blank). Shot 2, l12: Nandini picture-left, turned toward Pushpa but pitching the line past her; Tripathi soft in the background picture-right, under the shield.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [flatly] Madam, your transfer application has reached DSP sahab.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [cold] Where no FIR gets written, what is an SI for?

beats.action: Silent first, 2.0 s, no line: for 0.8 s she lifts the black desk-phone handset (coiled cord) from the SHO's desk; then shot 1, 1.2 s of push-button dial tones before l14: two-shot, Nandini picture-left with the handset at her ear, dialling, Tripathi picture-right with his right palm raised toward her to stop her, the peanut cone in his left hand; she dials anyway. Tripathi's objection is the picture; he has no line here. Shot 2, l14 and the first sentence of l15: close on Nandini, handset at her right ear, back of the handset to camera; the DSP is a phone voice only. Shot 3, on 'आपके ही थाने में': her eyes lift to the zero-crime shield on the wall (reverse insert of the shield). Shot 4, l16: back to her close.

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [sharply] A fake thana, in my area?

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [calm] Press conference at ten tomorrow, SI Joshi. In your own thana.

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [sharply] Before that, I want that man in the lockup.

beats.action: Silent 2.0 s in all, split in two. First 1.5 s, before l17: she puts the handset down (receiver click); shot 1, held: close on Tripathi; he has stopped chewing, a peanut halfway to his mouth. Shot 2, l17: single on Pushpa, already on her feet, knitting bag over her left shoulder, pushing the needles back into her bun. Shot 3, the other 0.5 s, silent, after l17 and before l18: Nandini turns to her (single), token on her right wrist. Shot 4, l18: close on Pushpa, steady, spectacles low.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [calm] I'll come with you, madam.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [quietly] I know the way.

beats.action: Afternoon, dusty light from the high windows. Silent first, shot 1: Nandini and Pushpa inside the lobby doors (Nandini picture-left, Pushpa picture-right with her knitting bag); Nandini sets the red helmet down on the complainants' bench, where it stays (s2e02 picks it up there). Shot 2, l19: close on Nandini. Shot 3, l20: Nirala at the counter does not argue or run; he pushes nine registers across, squared in one stack with a slip index on top, sleeves over his knuckles. Shot 4, l21: two-shot of Nirala and Pushpa, his open hand indicating the stair at the back; on the end of the line they nod to each other like colleagues.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] Seize every register.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] Registers one to nine, madam.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] The thickest file is upstairs, in the malkhana.

beats.action: Silent first, 2.5 s across two stills (about 1.5 s wide, 1.0 s insert). Shot 1, wide: the narrow projection room, afternoon light in shafts from the one small window; steel racks where film cans were now hold rows of sealed brown envelopes with red wax blobs and cloth-tied files, every tag painted blank; the old projector under its dust sheet. Shot 2: insert of Nandini's hands pulling down the thickest file, tied in red cloth, and untying it on the stool. Shot 3, l22: close on Nandini over the open file (pages painted blank). Nirala and Pushpa wait at the top of the stair, picture-right, soft focus, read as silhouettes only: the level cap, the bun with crossed needles.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [sharply] Thirty complaints. Ration fraud, extortion... every one names Bhaiyaji.

beats.action: ENDING, SPOKEN. Silent 5.0 s in all, in three places (silent_position takes one value, so the split is written here): 1.5 s after l24, 1.0 s after l25, 2.5 s after l26. Shot 1, l23: insert of the first complaint page, her right index finger under the top line (overlay ov_refusal_date: '17 मार्च'; it supports, it does not carry). Shot 2, l24: close on Nandini's face, reading aloud. Shot 3, silent 1.5 s after l24, two stills: her hand turns a page, the same top line on it; then her thumb riffling the edge of the stack, the same top line on each page in view (one or two other date overlays allowed). Shot 4, l25 begins: Pushpa's hands, her needles stopped mid-row; l25 ends on Nandini's close. Shot 5, silent 1.0 s after l25: insert, her right hand, token on its wrist, which was moving to the black handcuff pouch on her right hip, stops on it. Shot 6, l26: close on her face, eyes lifting from the file, to Pushpa or to no one. Hold 2.5 s after the line. Cut to black. STATE for s2e02 b1: her right hand still on the pouch, the token's string round that wrist, the red file open on the stool.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] Seventeenth March. 'I first went to Imlipur thana.'

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] 'SHO Tripathi said: FIR will not be written.'

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] All thirty of them... turned away by my own thana.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] So before ten tomorrow... who do I arrest?

sfx_notes: b1: big, hollow lobby room tone (high ceiling, terrazzo), a pigeon's wings somewhere high. The rubber stamp comes down once, a dry wooden thunk, in the 0.5 s before l01. Nothing under l01.
b2-b4: lobby tone continues; paper squared on the counter (b2); tea poured into a glass (b3); after l08 the lobby door swings shut behind her.
b5: open-air afternoon, the railway gate bell, a train horn, then a train rumbling past unseen; the kettle on the stall's coal stove. The horn peaks in the silence, never under a line.
b6-b9: slow ceiling fan in the real thana, flat and steady; peanut shells cracking under l09 and l10 (keep them small); knitting needles clicking under l11.

b8: handset lifted off its cradle (0.8 s), then push-button dial tones as she dials (1.2 s), over Tripathi's raised palm and before l14. The DSP's lines (l14-l16) through a phone filter: narrow band, faint line hiss, wide enough that consonants survive. Pull the fan and every other sound right down under all three DSP lines; no effect sits on top of a filtered word.
b9: receiver set down, a hard click. Then nothing: the chewing has stopped. Hold the fan alone for the stopped-peanut shot.
b10: the nine registers slide across the counter, one heavy paper thump.
b11: cloth knot pulled loose; a thick file opening; dust. Room tone smaller and closer than the lobby.

b12: one page turn, then the soft flutter of a thumb riffling the stack's edge (shot 3, the 1.5 s after l24). Pushpa's needles, faintly clicking since b11, stop before l25: the stop is the sound cue. Duck the bed to near silence under l26 so the cliffhanger is fully clear; nothing under it. After l26, 2.5 s of room tone, then cut to black on silence.
music_note: Deadpan small-town caper colour: a dry, sparse plucked figure (a single string instrument and soft hand percussion) enters only after l04 and sits under l05 in b4, drops out from l06 so the three punchlines (l06 to l08) play dry, comes back on b4's exit still, and returns under b10; never under a punchline and never mickey-mousing Nirala. No music at the crossing (b5): train and bell only. Out completely for the DSP call (b8) so the phone voice stays clear. From b11 a single low sustained note, barely audible, rising very slightly through b12; it ducks right down under l26 and cuts hard to silence on the cut to black. No sting on any line.
ending_question: Why did Tripathi turn away all thirty complaints against Bhaiyaji, and will Nandini, before ten tomorrow, put in the lockup the very man who wrote them down?
writer_notes: English adaptation (S5) of script.hi.json, not a literal translation. Same beats b1 to b12, same speakers, same line ids in the same order (l01 to l26; l13 does not exist in either file, it was cut in the Hindi and is not renumbered), same emotion tags in the same positions, same silent_seconds and silent_position per beat. Sources read: script.hi.json, the proof scripts' format (content/proof/photoreal/script.en.json), bible.json (the English names, the per-character English voice registers and the sample English key lines), D-016 and D-0M2 through a search tool. D-004, D-006, D-008, D-013 and D-014 were not read in full this session.

action, on_screen, location, locations, time_of_day, sfx_notes and music_note are copied unchanged from the Hindi script: picture, sound effects and music are shared between the two cuts. Two actions name a Hindi cue phrase; in the English cut they fall on these words: b6 shot 3 'Shield देखिए' is 'Look at the shield' (l09); b8 shot 3 'आपके ही थाने में' is 'In your own thana' (l15). The l23 overlay ov_refusal_date reads '17 March' in the English cut (bible overlay en value).

Registers follow the bible's English voice notes. Nandini: crisp, contracted, dry. Nirala: manual English, 'kindly', no contractions, articles dropped where a clerk would drop them ('then complaint', 'Thana has been stolen'). Tripathi: slow, keeps 'arre', the proverb shape of 'jahan... wahan' kept as 'Where there's no complaint, there's no crime.' Pushpa: short and plain, 'DSP sahab'. DSP: clipped, times and places. The complaint read aloud in l23 and l24 is written as an Indian complainant writes ('I first went to Imlipur thana', 'FIR will not be written').

Echo kept on purpose: l12 'Where no FIR gets written, what is an SI for?' answers l10's 'Where there's no complaint...' in the same shape, as 'जहाँ FIR ही नहीं...' answers 'जहाँ complaint नहीं...' in the Hindi. l25 uses 'turned away', the logline's phrase.

target_seconds are honest English estimates, not padded to the Hindi. They assume about 11 to 13 characters a second (10 for Tripathi, 14 for the DSP), plus about 0.3 s per sentence break and 0.5 s per ellipsis, which leans slow because Gate 0b measured real v4 takes 20 to 60 per cent over target. Spoken 98.5 s, silences 19.3 s, 12 speaker changes at 0.3 s (3.6 s): target_total_seconds 121.4 against 134.9 for the Hindi. Dialogue is about 1,080 characters by hand count (without tags); the 1,050 measure in D-016 direction 7 is defined on Hindi at about 10 characters a second, and English at 11 to 13 a second lands inside the same running time.

Lines more than about 15 per cent short of the Hindi target (English is simply quicker here; nothing was added to fill): l03 (3.4 vs 4.2), l06 (3.2 vs 4.0), l11 (4.8 vs 6.2), l14 (2.2 vs 2.8), l15 (4.8 vs 6.4), l19 (1.8 vs 2.2), l24 (3.8 vs 4.8), l25 (4.6 vs 5.4), l26 (4.4 vs 5.0). Under D-014 rule 6 the shots follow the measured English voice, so no shot needs a filler line; l15 is the one where the 'In your own thana' insert may come up sooner than in the Hindi cut.

Short turns to watch (budget 3 takes each): l18 'I know the way.' (15 characters), l19 'Seize every register.' (21), l14 (25), l02 (25), l01 (25; 'number' is kept as a carrier so the line is not two syllables). If l18 alone is unstable, rejoin l17 and l18 as in the Hindi writer note.

D-014: lines with an internal sentence break (l04, l05, l06, l09, l10, l15, l22, l23) will likely show a pause of 300 ms or more and be split into cue segments at the full stop. The ellipses in l22, l25 and l26 are deliberate pauses. Every line fits two subtitle lines of 32 graphemes or splits at a sentence break.

Pronunciation dictionary candidates for the English voices: thana (THAA-naa), Imlipur (IM-lee-poor), Nirala (ni-RAA-laa), Tripathi (tri-PAA-thee), Bhaiyaji (BHAI-yaa-jee), malkhana (maal-KHAA-naa, the police property room), arre (UH-ray), sahab (SAA-hab), Joshi (JO-shee); SI, SHO, FIR and DSP said as letters.

Tags: all Hindi tags kept on the same lines. '[deadpan]', '[cold]', '[flatly]' and '[earnest]' are in the verify group; if a cast voice ignores one, S10 swaps it for '[calm]' or '[quietly]'. The cliffhanger l26 is '[quietly]', low and fully voiced, never a whisper; sfx_notes already duck the bed under it. Only one '[quietly]' line sits in each beat that uses it.

Not verified: no JSON parser was run on this file (this session has no shell; the file was written by hand and the shared action, sfx and music strings were copied from script.hi.json through a search tool in pieces); no English take has been generated or timed; tag obedience on the cast voices is unknown; character counts and the hi/en id match were checked by hand only.
